newsitem.title: INDIA: India police act to douse trouble before Miss World.
newsitem.headline: India police act to douse trouble before Miss World.

text.p: Bangalore police said on Friday they would begin detaining militant activists ahead of the controversial Miss World beauty pageant, which has provoked threats of multiple suicide protests.
Police were tailing Kinay Narayana Shashikala, leader of a traditionalist women's group whose members said they would burn themselves alive if the show was held on Saturday in the south Indian city.
"Preventive arrests will start. We're keeping a close watch on the lady, Shashikala," police commissioner S.C. Burman told Reuters. "But we have not yet decided to detain her."

The law student has said 15 members of the Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakaening Women) would join the 20,000-member audience at Chinnaswamy cricket stadium, where Miss World is to be crowned, to carry out their threat of self-immolation.
Burman had no comment on a threat by a group calling itself the Indian Tigers that 400 activists would infiltrate the crowd and carry out lightning attacks inside and outside the stadium.

The Indian Tigers were unheard of until a few weeks ago when they attacked the Bangalore offices of the pageant's organisers, the Amitabh Bachchan Corp Ltd (ABCL), and claimed responsibility for a couple of small bomb blasts that injured no one.
"We are prepared for every eventuality," Burman said.
More than 10,000 security officers were expected to patrol the streets and stadium on Saturday.
Burman said he was concerned about trouble spoiling the three-hour extravaganza, which was expected to be watched by some two billion television viewers in 115 countries.
"I'm apprehensive, but that does not mean we're going to run away. I believe in looking the tiger in the eye," he said.
The state government has ordered schools and colleges to close on Friday and Saturday.

Banks and government offices were open, but the Hindu nationalist opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) called for a protest strike that was expected to mean transport stoppages and shop closures in some parts of the city.
Karanataka state chief minister J.H. Patel blasted the BJP for taking political mileage out of a beauty pageant when more pressing issues need to be addressed.
"The BJP has made it a political issue. They are desperate and lost sight of what has to be done," Patel said.
And in an editorial on Friday, The Pioneer newspaper reflected on the damage done to India's image by the furore.
"What started off as innocuous protest against alleged defilement of the Indian culture has degenerated into an exhibition of some perverse facets of the Indian mind," it said.
Meanwhile, the 88 contestants rested following their dress rehearsal on Thursday and ABCL's lawyers were hard at work trying to win last minute concessions from the Supreme Court in New Delhi.

They were trying to overturn restrictions placed on ABCL earlier this week by the Karnataka high court, which banned alchohol at the pageant and ruled that neither the army or border patrol forces could be used to protect the event.
